newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP to mull 10% cut in public works spending - paper.
newsitem.headline: LDP to mull 10% cut in public works spending - paper.

text.p: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) will consider cutting spending on public works projects by 10 percent for the 1998/99 year compared with the previous year, a Japanese business daily said on Monday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun quoted Taku Yamazaki, chairman of the LDP's policy-making committee, as making the remarks in a speech in northern Japan on Sunday.
The paper said that the plan to cut public works spending by 10 percent was likely to be included in broader plans on fiscal reform to be formed in March by the Japanese government and the LDP.
Japan plans to allocate about 9.7 trillion yen for public works projects in 1997/98. The fiscal year begins in April.
LDP officials were not immediately available for comment on the report.
